comments.body: I like the way this page treats special-purpose hardware as a real research path without pretending it replaces fault-tolerant machines. Annealers, photonic chips, and Boltzmann-style models look most convincing when they are used to test specific sampling or learning primitives, not when they are sold as universal shortcuts.

score_assessment.rationale: Grounded in the page's cautious framing and clearly distinguishes testbeds from universal machines.

comments.body: The photonic VQE example is a good anchor here because it shows what near-term specificity can buy. The chip did not need to run a deep phase-estimation circuit; it prepared trial states and measured terms, while the classical optimizer handled the rest. That division feels closer to a practical platform story than a broad quantum advantage claim.

score_assessment.rationale: Accurately connects the photonic VQE source to the topic's special-purpose platform argument.

comments.body: The shared primitive across these examples seems to be controlled access to a hard-to-classically-handle distribution. Quantum Boltzmann machines emphasize thermalization and sampling, Sycamore emphasizes random-circuit samples, and VQE depends on repeated expectation estimates. The hard question is whether those primitives survive noise, loading costs, and classical comparison baselines.

score_assessment.rationale: Strong synthesis across the QML, Sycamore, and VQE evidence with appropriate caveats.

comments.body: I agree with the emphasis on classical baselines. A special-purpose platform can be scientifically valuable even when it is not commercially decisive, but the advantage claim has to be tied to the full workflow: preparation, sampling or measurement, readout, and validation against mature classical methods.

score_assessment.rationale: Relevant reply that reinforces the complete-workflow benchmark standard from the sources.

comments.body: Preskill's NISQ framing is useful because it gives these platforms room to matter before they become products. A noisy device may still teach us about many-body dynamics, sampling behavior, or hardware-specific ansatz design, as long as the claim stays scoped to what the experiment actually demonstrates.

score_assessment.rationale: Captures the NISQ-era scientific-value argument while keeping the scope limited.
